From Middle English keye, kaye, keiȝe, from Old English cǣġ (“key, solution, experiment”) (whence also Scots key and kay (“key”)), from Anglo-Frisian Proto-West Germanic *kaiju, of uncertain origin. The only sure cognates are Saterland Frisian Koai (“key”), West Frisian kaai (“key”), and North Frisian kai, koie (“key”).
Variant of cay, from Spanish cayo, from Taíno cayo (“small island”)
Clipping of kilogram or kilo.
Clipping of key position.

senses.d: An object designed to open and close a lock or to activate or deactivate something, especially a length of metal inserted into a narrow opening on the lock to which it is matched (keyed).
ex: This key is to the backdoor.
insert the key into the lock (formal); put the key in the lock (informal)

senses.d: A card or fob that electronically signals a lock to open.
ex: My hotel room key is a card.
The gym will give you a fob that opens the door.

senses.d: A piece of information (e.g., a password or passphrase) used to encode or decode a message or messages.
A password restricting access to an IRC channel.
ex: if you know someone who is in the channel, you can query them and ask for the key.

senses.d: A key bump (A portion of a recreational drug in powdered form that is snorted from a key or similar small object.)
ex: I saw him snort a key at the party.

senses.d: Any of various tools comparable to a wrench (spanner) or driver, which have a specialized end that matches a fixture, analogously to a lock's key.
ex: The exterminator will bring a key thingy that can open the bait boxes.
Safe-deposit boxes open with a special key.

senses.d: A cotter pin.
A piece of wood used as a wedge.
The last board of a floor when laid down.
A keystone.
Indispensable, supremely important.
ex: He is the key player on his soccer team.
The enemy is moving troops through a key area. Distrupt their activities to open some holes in their defenses.

senses.d: Important, salient.
To fit (a lock) with a key.
To fit (pieces of a mechanical assembly) with a key to maintain the orientation between them.
To mark or indicate with a symbol indicating membership in a class.
To depress (a telegraph key).
To operate (the transmitter switch of a two-way radio).
(more usually to key in) To enter (information) by typing on a keyboard or keypad.
ex: Our instructor told us to key in our user IDs.

senses.d: To vandalize (a car, etc.) by scratching with an implement such as a key.
ex: He keyed the car that had taken his parking spot.

senses.d: To link (as one might do with a key or legend).
To be identified as a certain taxon when using a key.
To modify (an advertisement) so as to target a particular group or demographic.
One of a string of small islands.
A kilogram, especially of a recreational drug.
A key position player (a tall forward or defender).
